text:
sam_finops: FYI — daily FinOps dashboard is showing a ~+23% jump in EU GPU spend overnight, almost entirely concentrated in /v1/generate-gpt-small route. Not sure if this is traffic shift or a routing/provisioning change :chart_with_upwards_trend:

anya: ugh, can you drop the dashboard link and top-line numbers?

sam_finops: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/finops/dashboards/commitment-usage?date=2026-03-17
Top 3 by cost: /v1/generate-gpt-small = $18.2k, /v1/embed-long = $3.4k, /v1/chat-med = $1.1k

priya: copy. I also see increased average tokens per request for gpt-small yesterday (median went from 120 -> 540). Could be a prompt change in a customer pipeline.

mike_infra: infra note — there was a short i/o incident in us-west-2 at 02:10 UTC, we routed some traffic to eu-west-1 as fallback for ~25m. Autoscaler spun up more spots in the EU pool. That could explain both traffic spike and extra reserved usage.

infra-bot: Incident #INC-2026-034: fallback routing executed for 00:35–01:00 UTC. Autoscaler increased dedicated-pool-eu from 12 -> 20 GPUs at 02:35 UTC due to capacity pressure.

sam_finops: can we get the per-route cost query exported? putting it here to reproduce quickly:
```sql
SELECT route, model, SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd, SUM(tokens_in) AS tokens_in
FROM billing_events
WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND date = '2026-03-17'
GROUP BY route, model
ORDER BY cost_usd DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

priya: pasted output (top lines):
- /v1/generate-gpt-small | gpt-small-v2 | $18,215 | 4.9M tokens_in
- /v1/embed-long      | embed-long-v1 | $3,420  | 1.2M tokens_in
- /v1/chat-med        | chat-med-v1   | $1,120  | 180k tokens_in

anya: ok — this looks like usage, not a billing glitch. Two follow-ups: 1) which customers drove the long-token requests, 2) how much of this was charged to reserved vs on-demand.

sam_finops: customer breakdown shows 63% from 3 paying tenants (prod traffic), 37% from smaller test tenants. Reserved coverage dropped because autoscaler scaled beyond committed capacity; estimate of on-demand cost for the spike ~ $6.3k.

mike_infra: note on reserved capacity — our committed pool was sized based on weekly percentiles; sudden token-per-request increases can blow through headroom even if request-rate is steady. For EU we had 70% utilization baseline; rapid per-request size increases caused longer GPU occupancy.

priya: suggestion: add a quality gate metric to FinOps dash — tokens-per-request percentile by route. If P95 tokens crosses threshold, alert and propose temporary reservation hedge or traffic shaping.

anya: agreed. Also want a quick sim for hedging: what if we moved +8 GPUs into reserved EU capacity for Q2 vs buying on-demand during spikes. Can someone run a cost simulation?

sam_finops: running a quick sim — assumptions: reserved GPU monthly amortized = $3,200/GPU, on-demand marginal = $9.50/hr -> monthly equivalent ~ $6,840/GPU if used 24/7. Spike cost delta uses only hours above baseline. Rough output: 8 GPUs reserved for month saves ~ $12k if spike repeats weekly, breaks even otherwise. Will push full calc to the dashboard.

mike_infra: operational constraint: we have 6 GPUs in backfill capacity in eu region that are shared with other pools. If we convert them to reserved we lose some flexibility. Need approval from product ops for impact.

infra-bot: Action created: FINOPS-2026-55 — "EU reserved hedge simulation + approval" assigned to sam_finops, due 2026-03-20.

priya: for short term mitigation, can we apply a per-route soft quota on /v1/generate-gpt-small for non-enterprise tenants? throttle those to avoid burning on-demand?

anya: yes, apply throttling to test tenants and send a heads-up to the 3 big customers before we do anything. Also add a per-model P95 tokens alert to the FinOps dash.

sam_finops: noted. I'll update the dashboard, attach the full sim and a recommended commit level (6–10 GPUs) and a cost/benefit table by end of day. Thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
